tests.rationale: Runs a keyed event-time sliding window built from the documented two-argument default factory and asserts event-time-only semantics: the slide-aligned [0, 5000) window fires with all five records, every window spans the configured size (not the slide), and overlapping windows are one slide interval apart. tests.coverage_target: solution.patch sliding allowed-lateness default and runtime lateness-read paths (SlidingTimeWindowStrategy constructor + WindowUtils sliding getAllowedLateness)
tests.rationale: Two event-time jobs pin the FLIP lateness contract for sliding windows through the public late-record callback. Job A (two-argument default, zero lateness) requires an out-of-order record whose window has already closed to reach onLateRecord; a constructor that substitutes the slide interval for the default lateness keeps the window open and reports no late record. Job B (four-argument factory, three seconds lateness) requires the same record to remain inside its still-open window; a runtime that reads the configured lateness as zero expires the window early and reports the record as late instead.

tests.coverage_target: solution.patch tumbling/sliding allowed-lateness runtime paths reached only by event-time late-record jobs
tests.rationale: A tumbling window configured with three seconds of allowed lateness keeps [0, 5000) open at watermark 5500, so the ts=4000 record stays in-window (record count == 1) and is never late (late count == 0). A runtime that reads the tumbling lateness as zero, or a one-input BuiltinFuncs wrapper that forwards zero, expires the window early and reports the record as late.

tests.coverage_target: solution.patch tumbling/sliding allowed-lateness runtime paths reached only by event-time late-record jobs
tests.rationale: With zero lateness the [0, 5000) window cleans up at maxTimestamp 4999. A second ts=4999 record arrives exactly at watermark 4999 (cleanupTime == watermark, timestamp == watermark). The inclusive (<=) window-late and element-late contract routes it to onLateRecord exactly once; a strict (<) boundary for either predicate accepts the record and emits no late record.
